title: Convergence of phyllotactic ratios to the golden mean has no biological significance

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Convergence of phyllotactic ratios to the golden mean has no biological significance

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: That the phyllotactic fractions 1/2, 2/3, 3/5… converge to 0.618…, the golden mean, is a mathematical coincidence without biological significance; the precise divergence angle and orthostichies are likewise unimportant.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And lastly, the fact that the successional numbers, expressed as fractions, 1/2, 2/3, 3/5, represent a convergent series, whose final term is equal to 0·61803..., the _sectio aurea_ or “golden mean” of unity, is seen to be a mathematical coincidence, devoid of biological significance

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Divergence angle and the golden mean”. Scope: spiral phyllotaxis

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-10: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing plant data can refute or support specific adaptive explanations, but Thompson's unrestricted absence claim is not operationally bounded. Any observed pattern can be redescribed without settling whether it is 'significant.'

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The mathematical convergence is demonstrable, but 'no biological significance' has no unique measurable consequence without specifying a biological function or causal model. Particular hypotheses, such as improved packing or light interception near the golden angle, can be tested, but no finite dataset can exclude every significance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The exact numerical convergence is a mathematical fact rather than an empirical claim.

Biological significance is undefined and ranges over unlimited possible functions.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The convergence of those fractions to the golden mean is mathematics, and the further assertion that the convergence has no biological significance is an interpretation of that mathematics. Phyllotactic counts are compatible with the coincidence reading and with models in which the golden angle is an attractor of growth. No dataset outcome decides which reading is the significant one without an extra definition the claim does not supply.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The continued-fraction limit of 1/2, 2/3, 3/5, … is an arithmetic fact about those fractions. Calling the limit biologically insignificant, and the precise divergence unimportant, does not state a measurement that would separate a coincidence from a developmental attractor, because both accounts produce the same sequence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Biological significance is not defined as a variable or a decision threshold.

A packing optimum, a dynamical attractor, and a mathematical coincidence can leave identical parastichy counts.
